# Film Burn

**Light › Burn** · v1.0.0 · 48 frames at 30 fps (24–100)

Holes burn through the old scene with glowing edges until the frame is white-hot, then it cools to reveal the new scene.

[Preview video](https://github.com/GTKottman/remotion-transitions/releases/download/media/film-burn@1.0.0.mp4) · [Alpha overlay for editing apps](https://github.com/GTKottman/remotion-transitions/releases/download/media/film-burn@1.0.0-overlay.mov)

## Where it is used

- Vintage and film looks
- Endings
- Music videos

## Use it

```tsx
import { linearTiming, TransitionSeries } from '@remotion/transitions';
import { toPresentation } from './src/core';
import filmBurn from './transitions/09-light/burn/film-burn';

<TransitionSeries.Transition
  presentation={toPresentation(filmBurn, { /* params */ })}
  timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 48 })}
/>
```

Use `linearTiming`: the transition applies its own easing. It draws with WebGL, so render with `--gl=angle` (GPU) or `--gl=swangle` (no GPU).

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `glow` | color | `"#FF6A00"` |  | Colour of the burning edge. |
| `core` | color | `"#FFF4E0"` |  | Colour of the burnt-through centre. |
| `seed` | integer | `1` | 0–9999 | Changes the random layout. |
| `hold` | number | `0.04` | 0–0.3 | Share of the transition at full burn. |
